final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest EVEscape escape score with strong structural compatibility and good sequence plausibility; likely disrupts m102.4 epitope while preserving fold.
High escape score and acceptable structural compatibility, with some natural MSA tolerance; conservative alanine change mitigates viability risk.
High escape score but only moderate structural compatibility and marginal sequence plausibility; retained as third option with tempered confidence.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the top-3 ordering or candidate membership.

history.rationale: Surface-exposed polar residue near the m102.4/receptor-binding interface; removing the hydroxyl may disrupt antibody contacts while preserving ephrin binding.
Small polar-to-alanine substitution likely lowers antibody polar contacts while maintaining backbone flexibility and receptor-binding compatibility.
Excellent structural compatibility (0.936) and sequence plausibility (0.931) but low escape score (0.552). Retained as a conservative fallback.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution that may alter side-chain packing recognized by m102.4 without abolishing receptor binding.
Leu-to-Phe increases side-chain bulk; could sterically obstruct antibody binding but carries moderate risk of receptor-site perturbation.
Poor structural compatibility (0.348) and low escape score (0.515); not competitive.

rejection.reason: Poor structural compatibility (0.348) and low escape score (0.515); not competitive.

history.rationale: Smaller hydrophobic residue in a loop likely contacted by m102.4; may reduce antibody fit while maintaining local structure.
Conservative smaller hydrophobic change that may alter an epitope surface while preserving core packing nearby.
Very low structural compatibility (0.199) despite good sequence plausibility and moderate escape score; likely non-viable.

rejection.reason: Very low structural compatibility (0.199) despite good sequence plausibility and moderate escape score; likely non-viable.

history.rationale: Charge reversal at a surface acidic position could strongly reduce m102.4 binding, though may carry some structural risk.
Charge reversal may strongly disrupt antibody recognition, but is less conservative and could impair receptor binding or folding.
Low escape score (0.446) and only moderate structure (0.525); charge reversal likely too disruptive.

rejection.reason: Low escape score (0.446) and only moderate structure (0.525); charge reversal likely too disruptive.

history.rationale: Very conservative change in an epitope-adjacent residue; likely to preserve folding and receptor binding while subtly altering antibody recognition.
Conservative hydrophobic substitution in a likely m102.4 epitope region; retains side-chain volume and likely minimizes receptor-binding disruption.
Decent escape score (0.698) with high structural compatibility (0.774) and perfect sequence plausibility (1.0). Conservative substitution likely preserves receptor binding.
Loss of the tyrosine hydroxyl without changing aromatic character; may reduce polar antibody contacts while retaining receptor interaction.
Phe/Tyr change removes a hydrogen-bonding hydroxyl while preserving aromatic character, potentially reducing antibody contact without major receptor-binding loss.
Similar escape score to I510V (0.696) with good structure (0.815) and sequence plausibility (0.910). Retained as a high-viability alternative.
Removes a charged side chain in a solvent-exposed loop region that may be part of the m102.4 epitope.
Removes a charged side chain that may be involved in antibody salt bridges; may affect receptor binding if this residue contributes electrostatically.
High escape score (0.830) but very poor structural compatibility (0.220) and weak sequence plausibility (0.606), suggesting likely disruption of receptor-binding fold.

rejection.reason: High escape score (0.830) but very poor structural compatibility (0.220) and weak sequence plausibility (0.606), suggesting likely disruption of receptor-binding fold.

history.rationale: Charge-removing substitution near the C-terminal receptor-binding loop; could disrupt antibody interaction while mostly preserving backbone.
Charge-removing substitution near the C-terminus; plausible escape mutation but possible impact on local stability or receptor contacts.
High escape score (0.835) and acceptable structural compatibility (0.739). MSA shows some natural tolerance (0.333) despite low coverage.
Changes both charge and shape at a likely m102.4 contact residue; possible escape but higher receptor-binding risk.
Polar-to-basic substitution at the extreme C-terminus may alter antibody epitope but carries uncertainty for receptor-binding preservation.
Strong EVEscape escape score (0.863) with high structural compatibility (0.875) and good sequence plausibility (0.855). Likely to disrupt m102.4 epitope while preserving fold.
Terminal residue likely solvent-exposed; removing the threonine side chain may affect antibody contacts with minimal global disruption.
Small terminal substitution may have limited escape benefit; retained as a lower-priority candidate pending structural/evolution evidence.
High escape score (0.801) with moderate structural compatibility (0.630). Sequence plausibility is marginal (0.558), so confidence is tempered.
